good afternoon colleagues and welcome to a quick tour of the ascent and rcmi faculty development and support opportunities so who are we and what do we do ascent supports student research and training but also faculty development on the research and teaching level and there is support for institutional infrastructure in terms of core laboratories and animal research facilities rcmi a research center for minority institution at morgan the center for urban health and disparities urban health disparities research and innovation is led by dr hong tao yu and focuses on health disparities research faculty research support is included faculty research development as well as co-laboratories and outreach centers so what funding opportunities are available they are pilot research grants for biomedical biobehavioral projects ranging from 20 to 50 000 for up to two years they are community-based participatory research funding opportunities they are summer collaborative research sabbaticals at local r1 are one institutions and who's eligible eligible are tenure truck faculty at any rank and msu research faculty at any rank let me tell you about upcoming workshops first there is on august 18th mentoring in higher education hosted by dr laurie laura dorsey elson and please look at msu announce and other locations for the registration link on the flyer there is the intermediate grant writing workshop which starts september the 11th and goes through the middle of december this is designed to help participants particularly this help participants prepare for pilot brand proposals and it's a very hands-on workshop focused on the preparation of the proposal in the workshop it meets online on zoom and on canvas on thursday nights and it is open to all faculty postdoctoral trainees and senior doctoral students so this one not just for tenure stream faculty it is first come first serve registration and the enrollment is limited there is our upcoming seminar fall seminar series for interdisciplinary seminar on thursday from 4 to 5 30 and it will continue on zoom 4 this fall intermediary interdisciplinary topics are catering to both students and faculty audiences and we have external and internal speakers the focus is on health disparities and urban health and it is a great networking tool because we have an open discussion after the formal presentation speaker suggestions will be accepted for future seasons let me talk a little bit more about the pilot grant and cbpr funding applications will be due in january 2022 for summer 2022 funding and let me point out that new investigators must first complete the intermediate grant writing workshop before they can apply for these mechanisms ascent applicants must be new investigators rcmi applicants must be either new investigators or new to health disparities research the application follows the nih r21 format and applications must meet nih mission and must be aligned with specific nih institutes these will be externally reviewed by experts in the field using the nih review criteria competitive applications must thereafter meet nih program approval collaborative summer research sabbaticals are designed to expand the research capacity of the msu investigator they are designed to lead to long-lasting collaborations and should result in a grant proposal or publication with a collaborating group the topic must be health-related and within the nih mission and these are internally reviewed by an msu committee and rated based on a rubric and then funded based on ranking look out for detailed information flyers on the ascent rcmi and academic affairs canvas site please and for more information you can contact equine pinchback morgan.edu also look out please for presentation for the presentation by my colleague dr james bachira and his team on core facilities and services i hope you have a good rest of your faculty institute you
